scenes.headline: How a seven-line loop embeds a search query
scenes.sub: Chrome's Modern Web Guidance, read and re-run
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Tindra! Chrome's Modern Web Guidance swapped a twenty-three megabyte transformer for a table and a sum.

scenes.title: The loop, one row at a time

steps.term: Static embedding: one fixed vector per word
steps.say: The table has one row per word. Twenty-nine thousand words, two hundred fifty-six small integers each.
A query lights up its words' rows. Animate, height, auto.
Each row is scaled by one number, its weight, and added into the output. Three words, seven hundred sixty-eight multiply-adds.
Normalize it, and compare with every guide. The guides were embedded once, by Gemini, at release time.
Every word gets a row. Fetch priority is one word here, not four fragments.
Gemini embeds each word alone, and keeps the first two hundred fifty-six dimensions.

steps.term: Tokenlearn: fit word sums to whole-query embeddings
steps.say: Then the rows are tuned, so word sums land where Gemini puts the whole query.
Last, each row is squeezed into bytes, its scale folded into its weight.

scenes.title: What one embed costs
scenes.say: On my M1 Max, the loop itself takes about one microsecond. A cold single call takes about twenty-five, close to Google's thirty.

scenes.label: agent-eval Hit@10, replayed from the public queries
scenes.say: Replaying the public agent queries, the right guide is in the top ten ninety-nine point four percent of the time. Exactly Google's number.

states.say: But the out-of-scope set has ninety queries like jest mocks and Kubernetes.
Rejected: none. Every one gets ten guides.
